 Cam Spencer

 Cam Spencer, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey will start Saturday’s game against the Kings. 
 The Grizzlies are without Ty Jerome, who’s out with a back injury. Spencer will start at point guard, and with Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) also out, he’ll likely log heavy minutes. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Source:  Memphis Grizzlies

 Ty Jerome (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings. 
 Jerome will miss a game for the first time this season. His absence likely means Cam Spencer will start, especially with Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) also out. Spence is worth streaming due to the absences. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome struggled on Thursday and finished with just 10 points (3-of-12 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, two steals and one three-pointer against the Trail Blazers. 
 Less than an hour before tipoff, it was reported that Jerome was questionable for this game with back tightness. Despite the flare up, he was able to start, though it ended up being his worst performance of the season, and he only played 24 minutes. This is worth keeping an eye on, especially ahead of their next game against the Kings on Saturday. Cam Spencer and Scotty Pippen Jr. would fill out the point guard minutes if Jerome were unavailable. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer (back) and Ty Jerome (ankle) are out for Friday’s game against the Jazz. 
 The Grizzlies will once again be without Spencer and Jerome, which limits their perimeter depth. Javon Small and Walter Clayton Jr. are questionable; they’ll be handling the playmaking responsibilities on Friday if available. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer (back) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Nuggets. 
 After logging 21 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Cavaliers, Spencer is back on the sidelines for Wednesday’s game. Walter Clayton Jr., who played 25 minutes off the bench, should return to the starting lineup. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer (back) is off the injury report for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Spencer is back after sitting out Sunday’s loss to the Bucks. His return may result in fewer minutes for Lucas Williamson, who played 36 minutes in Milwaukee. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome (ankle) and Cam Spencer (back) are out for Sunday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Jerome will remain out for a seventh straight game, while Spencer will miss a second due to his back injury. With Javon Small also out, the Grizzlies will rely heavily on Walter Clayton Jr. if he’s able to return from a hip injury that kept him out of Friday’s loss to the Raptors. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer (back) and Ty Jerome (ankle) are out for Friday’s game against the Raptors. 
 While Spencer was in the Grizzlies’ starting lineup for Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks, Jerome has missed the team’s last six games, counting Friday’s matchup with the Raptors. Memphis will lean heavily on Javon Small and Walter Clayton Jr., with the former already in the starting lineup. 
 Javon Small 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #10 
 Javon Small recorded 13 points (4-of-5 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks. 
 Inactive for Monday’s loss to the Suns, Small was inserted into the Grizzlies’ starting lineup on Wednesday. While he did shoot the ball well, the overall impact was somewhat muted. Cam Spencer (10/1/8/1 with one three-pointer) and Walter Clayton Jr. (10/1/5 with two three-pointers) are under standard contracts while Small remains on a two-way deal, making them safer options for managers considering which to add off the waiver wire. 
 Javon Small 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #10 
 Javon Small (back) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Small missed Monday’s game against Phoenix, but he will return to take on New York. Cam Spencer started in his place for that game, but he will return to playing a role off the bench with Small back in the mix. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome (ankle) has been ruled out against the Knicks on Wednesday. 
 Jerome will miss a fifth straight game, which means Cam Spencer, Javon Small and Walter Clayton Jr. will continue to fill the point guard minutes. Small will be back after a one-game absence, so he should start, with the other two coming off the bench.

 Kyle Kuzma amassed 14 points (6-of-12 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
 Kuzma’s shot 50 percent or better from the field in four of his last five appearances, solid efficiency for a player who hasn’t been known for that in the past. However, the overall stat line probably wasn’t enough to convince managers in 12-team leagues to consider adding Kuzma. The Bucks open a four-game Week 3 on Monday against the Timberwolves. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Myles Turner produced 10 points (4-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
 Turner had his hands full with Cleveland’s Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, who combined for 52 points and 16 rebounds. Milwaukee’s veteran center recorded a complete stat line, but the value was a bit limited beyond the rebounds and blocks. Kel’el Ware (19/10/3/1/2 with three-pointers) finished with a better stat line, but he played 12 of his 24 minutes in the fourth quarter after the outcome was no longer in doubt. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Tyler Herro finished Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers with 15 points (5-of-18 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers.
 This wasn’t Herro’s best night, as he shot 1-of-7 from inside the arc. While the four three-pointers will please some fantasy managers, the overall output was disappointing. However, given the gap between the Bucks and Cavaliers, it wasn’t all that surprising. Herro will look to bounce back on Monday when the Bucks visit the Timberwolves. Milwaukee plays four games next week. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 James Harden accumulated 13 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
 With the Cavaliers getting dominant efforts from Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, they didn’t need much from Harden or Donovan Mitchell (15/4/3 with two three-pointers) on Saturday. However, fantasy managers rostering either guard likely hoped for more production. Harden played 26 minutes on Saturday, checking out for the last time with 2:45 remaining in the third quarter. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jarrett Allen tallied 25 points (12-of-16 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists and one steal in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
 Not only did Allen record his first double-double of the season on Saturday, but the 25 points were a season-high for the Cavaliers’ center. He scored 19 of his 25 points in the first half, shooting 9-of-12 from the field. Shooting 65.5 percent from the field thus far, Allen has provided greater value than many fantasy managers expected before the season began. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Evan Mobley finished Saturday’s win over the Bucks with 27 points (11-of-16 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers.
 Cleveland removed most of the drama from Saturday’s game with a 48-point second quarter, led by Mobley. Shooting 5-of-5 from the field, he scored 13 points in the quarter, and frontcourt sidekick Jarrett Allen added nine. Mobley played just one minute in the fourth quarter, or his stat line could have been more robust. The Cavaliers play four games next week, starting with the undermanned Thunder on Monday (home) and Wednesday (away). 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker accounted for 12 points (3-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.
 Alexander-Walker had a rough night in New Orleans, missing all six of his three-point attempts. As a result, his streak of five straight games with at least two three-pointers to begin the season ended. Add in the lackluster assist and steal production, and this was a tough night for fantasy managers rostering Alexander-Walker. He’ll look to bounce back on Monday against the Pacers. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Johnson (ankle) recorded 13 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.
 Johnson played the entire third quarter, but that would be the last we’d see of him on the court Saturday night. The Hawks forward sprained his left ankle, and while Johnson was questionable to return, he didn’t, as the game got out of hand. Atlanta’s four-game Week 3 begins on Monday against the Pacers and includes a back-to-back. If Johnson misses time, Aaron Wiggins (10/2/1/1/1 with two three-pointers) could become more important. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 CJ McCollum finished Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans with 14 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Playing in New Orleans for the first time since he was traded to Washington in the summer of 2025, McCollum had a relatively quiet Saturday night. The field-goal percentage was good, but CJ’s overall stat line was a bit lean. The Hawks lost Jalen Johnson to a sprained ankle in the second half, and McCollum may be needed to produce more offensively if the star forward misses time. Atlanta plays four games next week, starting with Indiana on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Zion Williamson 
 NOP 
 Forward

 Player Stats

 Zion Williamson accumulated 15 points (5-of-8 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, four assists and three steals in Saturday’s win over the Hawks.
 While Williamson’s defensive effort has been questioned at times, he’s provided consistent value in steals this season. He’s had at least two in each of the Pelicans’ first six games and is averaging 3.2 per game. His most productive season was 2024-25, when Zion averaged 1.2 steals per game. This early production is definitely out of the norm for him, so fantasy managers should plan for a likely decrease at some point. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
